## What it is

A personal digital voice hotspot: a **Raspberry Pi 5** with a **duplex MMDVM
hat**, running [**WPSD**](https://w0chp.radio/wpsd/). It puts a low-power
digital voice access point on my desk, so a handheld can reach the digital voice
networks without needing to be in range of a repeater.

Being duplex, it transmits and receives simultaneously on separate frequencies,
so it behaves like a miniature repeater rather than imposing the turn-taking a
simplex hotspot requires. It gives me access to both the **DMR** and **YSF**
(System Fusion) networks, and works with the FT5D handheld and the FTM-200DE in
the shack.

It appears in my radios' memory files as the `G0LFT HOTSPOT` channel: 438.725
MHz receive, 434.725 MHz transmit, in Fusion (`DN`) mode with the wide IF
filter, which C4FM needs to decode reliably.

## Why I built it

Cambridge has repeater coverage, but a hotspot removes the dependency entirely.
It works from indoors, at very low power, and lets me move between the digital
voice networks without retuning anything. It's also the most convenient way to
experiment with the digital modes, since reflectors and talkgroups become a
configuration change rather than a drive to somewhere with coverage.

It's the piece of infrastructure that made the digital side of the hobby
practical for me day to day, which is why the wide-IF discovery it prompted
ended up baked into my [memory-channel builder](radio-memory-builder.qmd).

## Current status & goals

- **Built and in daily use**, running WPSD on a Pi 5 with a duplex MMDVM hat.
- Gives access to the **DMR** and **YSF** networks.
- Works with the FT5D handheld and the FTM-200DE via the same `G0LFT HOTSPOT`
  memory channel.
